jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Specialist I/II
jobs.description:
**The Position**
----------------

Under direct or general supervision, performs a variety of technical to complex monitoring inspection, and compliance in the administration of the Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA), which implements hazardous materials business plan, hazardous waste generators, onsite hazardous waste treatment, underground storage tanks, Aboveground Petroleum Storage (APSA), and California Accidental Release Prevention Program (CalARP) programs; identifies violations of codes and regulations, ;conducts field inspections; collects and records data; prepares reports; maintains a variety of records and files; and performs related duties as assigned.
  
  
**Distinguishing Characteristics**
  
***Hazardous Materials Specialist I****:* This is the entry-level classification in the Hazardous Materials Specialist series. Initially under close supervision, incumbents with basic experience learn City systems, operations, practices, and procedures. As experience is gained, assignments become more varied, complex, and difficult; close supervision and frequent review of work lessen as an incumbent demonstrates skill to perform the work independently. Positions at this level usually perform most of the duties required of the positions at the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level but are not expected to function at the same skill level and usually exercise less independent discretion and judgment in matters related to work procedures and methods. Work is usually supervised while in progress and fits an established structure or pattern. Exceptions or changes in procedures are explained in detail as they arise.
  
  
***Hazardous Materials Specialist II****:* This is the journey-level classification in the Hazardous Materials Specialist series. Positions at this level are distinguished from the Hazardous Materials Specialist I-level by the performance of the full range of duties as assigned, working independently, and exercising judgment and initiative. Positions at this level receive only occasional instruction or assistance as new or unusual situations arise and are fully aware of the operating procedures and policies of the work unit.
  
  
Positions in the Hazardous Materials Specialist class series are flexibly staffed; positions at the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level are normally filled by advancement from the Hazardous Materials Specialist I-level; progression to the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level is dependent on (i) management affirmation that the position is performing the full range of duties assigned to the classification; (ii) satisfactory work performance; (iii) the incumbent meeting the minimum qualifications for the classification including any licenses and certifications; and (iv) management approval for progression to the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level.
  
  
**Supervision Exercised and Received**:
  
Receives direct supervision (Hazardous Materials Specialist I) or general supervision (Hazardous Materials Specialist II) from the Hazardous Materials Supervisor. Exercises no direct supervision over staff.

**Duties and Responsibilities**
-------------------------------

**Examples of Typical Job Functions**
  
*The typical job functions of the classification may include, but are not limited to, the functions below and are subject to changes in operational necessity.*
  
*Positions at the I-level may perform some of these duties and responsibilities in a learning capacity.*

* Performs routine and non-routine inspections and associated technical tasks in the administration and implementation of the City’s Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA) program which include: Aboveground Petroleum Storage Act (APSA); Area Plans for hazardous materials emergencies; California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) for extremely hazardous substances, including toxic and flammable materials; Hazardous Materials Business Plans for onsite handling of hazardous materials; Hazardous Waste/Universal Waste Generator and Onsite Hazardous Waste Treatment; and Underground Storage Tanks.
* Responds to and investigates inquiries/complaints and agency referrals related to the handling, storage, or disposal of hazardous materials .
* Communicates with facility representatives about regulatory violations, enforcement actions, waste minimization and industrial and commercial stormwater controls..
* Reviews Risk Management Plans and inspects and audits industrial facilities covered under the California Accidental Release Program.
* Reviews Hazardous Materials Business Plans and Hazardous Waste Generator Registrations submitted through the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable state and federal codes and regulations.
* Conducts plan reviews for new construction/alteration to ensure compliance with applicable codes and regulations including the hazardous materials provisions of the California Fire Code.
* Permits, inspects, and oversees the installation and removal of underground hazardous materials storage tank systems.
* Perform related duties as required.

**Qualifications**
------------------

**Experience and Education Guidelines**
  
*Any combination equivalent to experience and education that would most likely provide the required knowledge and abilities would be qualifying. A typical way to obtain the knowledge and abilities would be:*
  
  
**Education**: Educational requirements as specified in **California Code of Regulations, Title 27 §15260****.** Equivalent to graduation from an accredited college or university or equivalent degree with major course work in one of the following disciplines of biology or microbiology, chemistry, chemical engineering, physics, physical science, environment science, geology or soil science, environmental health, environmental or sanitary engineering, toxicology, industrial hygiene, hazardous materials management, fire science or fire technology.
  
  
**

Environmental Scientist

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) and Cannabis Program Manager, the Environmental Scientist performs professional scientific analyses and fieldwork associated with appropriate use of pesticides and supports DPR’s Cannabis Program. Applies scientific methods and principles to perform environmental investigations, analyses, research and studies for compliance with toxic and hazardous pesticide restrictions. Provides oversight of enforcement compliance to maintain statewide uniformity. Incumbent generates, analyzes and evaluates scientific data for regulatory compliance with human health and environmental requirements, providing protections from pesticide use on human health, non-target vegetation, cannabis cultivation, food safety, surface/ground water, wildlife, and air quality.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The incumbent works in a single-floor building under artificial lighting. The collection of samples as indicated for this position requires the ability to lift and carry a minimum of 40 pounds, bend, squat, and climb over boxes, containers, or pallets; travel by automobile or air may be required to different areas of the State. There is field work performed requiring the ability to maneuver over uneven ground and work in outdoor conditions. Occasional statewide travel may be required. Occasional irregular work schedules may be required. Travel may include overnight stays several days each month.
  
  
**NOTE:** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Environmental Scientist, Science and Public Health Partnerships
jobs.description:
**Overview**
------------

**Work Type:** Ongoing - Full-time

**Salary:** $193,946 - $263,771

**Grade:** VPS 7

**Occupation:** Science and research

**Location:** Melbourne - Northern suburbs

**Reference:** 1831

**Role details:** Ongoing, full time | VPS 7 | $193,946 to $263,771 + 12% superannuation | Centre for Applied Sciences, Ernest Jones Drive, Macleod VIC 3085

  

* **Shape Victoria’s environmental science and public health strategy**
* **Build high-value research, government and industry partnerships**
* **Translate leading science and research into regulatory innovation**
  

**About the organisation**

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is Victoria’s environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on Victorians and their environment. EPA is a values and purpose-driven organisation that works with community, government and industry to deliver for all Victorians. As an independent statutory authority, EPA uses its powers and tools to prevent risks to the environment and human health.

  

**About the role**

As Deputy Chief Environmental Scientist, Science and Public Health Strategy and Partnerships, you will lead EPA’s Science Strategy, Partnerships and Public Health branch, driving sustainable operations and partnerships, technical leadership of science research and development strategy, regulatory innovation and environmental public health influence. Reporting to the Chief Environmental Scientist, you will provide senior executive support and strategic advice on complex science, public health and partnership matters, and represent EPA externally when required. You will provide executive sponsorship for EPA’s Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation model, build high-value partnerships across universities, research institutes, government, industry and health agencies, and lead the development of EPA’s science, digital innovation and environmental public health strategies. Taking a One Health lens, you will integrate science, engineering and research capabilities to strengthen environmental and public health outcomes.

  

**About you**

You are an established scientific and environmental public health leader with extensive experience integrating multidisciplinary health, environmental science and engineering disciplines to translate evidence into strategy and action. You have demonstrated senior executive leadership experience in a complex scientific, public health or regulatory environment and the capability to act as a trusted deputy to a chief scientist or equivalent executive. You bring experience developing strategy, establishing priorities, managing risk and translating strategic direction into practical delivery, together with experience in major research programs, centres of excellence or strategic partnership models. You can influence senior stakeholders, negotiate complex outcomes and clearly communicate scientific, environmental public health and strategic issues to executive, governing board, government, partners and public audiences. A doctorate or relevant postgraduate qualification in environmental public health or a related discipline is required.

jobs.title: Principal Consultant / Technical Director - Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment
jobs.description:
**Principal Consultant / Technical Director – Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment**

  

Lead Technical Excellence. Shape Strategy. Grow a Market-Leading Practice.

Are you an established **Ecotoxicologist or Ecological Risk Assessor** looking for an opportunity to build your profile, influence major projects, and help shape the future direction of a growing environmental consultancy practice?

  

We are seeking an experienced **Principal Consultant or Technical Director** to join and lead our **Ecotoxicology and Ecological Risk Assessment group as part of the Toxicology & Risk team** . This is a key technical and business role for a recognised industry professional with a strong technical reputation, established client relationships, and a passion for growing business and developing people.

  

As a key member within our **Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology and Risk Practice** , you will work alongside a highly regarded team of specialist consultants, including a dedicated ecotoxicology group and a broader multidisciplinary practice of more than 40+ experts across Asia Pacific.

  

This is more than a technical leadership role. It is an opportunity to join a collaborative team that combines deep technical expertise with a strong growth mindset. You will have the autonomy to shape the direction of the ecotoxicology practice while being supported by a substantial multidisciplinary network of specialists who are solving some of the most complex environmental challenges across the region.

  

We have just over 1,200 staff in Asia Pacific and you will find us located in all the major cities and many regional areas. We are open to location for the successful person where we have established offices in place.

  

**Responsibilities**

Working with other technical specialists who are passionate about their fields and highly collaborative employees, this role offers the platform to:

  

* Lead and grow a successful ecotoxicology and ecological risk assessment capability.
* Drive business development and work-winning initiatives across existing and emerging markets.
* Leverage your professional network and industry profile to identify opportunities and develop long-term client partnerships.
* Provide technical leadership on complex environmental, contaminated land, mining, industrial, infrastructure and regulatory projects.
* Mentor and develop a team of talented ecotoxicologists and risk assessment specialists.
* Collaborate with leading experts across contaminated land, geochemistry, toxicology, human health risk assessment, hydrogeology and environmental sciences.
Influence strategic direction, service offerings and market growth within a well-established environmental consulting business.  

  

**Experience**

Not only will you be a honest, trusted and great person to be around, you will also be a recognised technical leader who brings:

  

* Relevant tertiary qualifications in ecotoxicology, environmental science, ecology, toxicology or a related discipline coupled with 10-15+ years’ experience ( *ideally within a consulting environment but open to other industry)*
* A strong reputation within industry, regulatory, government and/or commercial sectors.
* Demonstrated success in winning work, developing client relationships and generating revenue growth.
* Established networks and connections that can contribute to the continued expansion of the practice.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and mentoring technical professionals.
* Strong commercial acumen and the ability to identify and capitalise on market opportunities.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.  

  

**Our Benefits**

We are most proud of our expert teams and unique culture where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients.

  

Whether you’re enjoying our flexible hybrid work environment, taking advantage of our novated leasing offers, or at a time in your life where a supportive and generous parental leave scheme is key, our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

  

You can find a comprehensive list **here.**

  

**Next Steps**

If leading an established and premier team at a global multidisciplinary consultancy is your next career move, apply now with a copy of your CV and cover letter.

  

*Unsolicited resumes from recruitment consultants will not be accepted. You must be part of the preferred supplier agreement list which is coordinated through our Talent Acquisition team.*

jobs.title: Environmental Program Leader – Hazardous Waste and Dangerous Goods Compliance
jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

The Environmental Program Leader – Hazardous Waste and Dangerous Goods Compliance will provide enterprise leadership, technical expertise, and continuous improvement across hazardous waste management and dangerous goods/hazmat transportation. In this highly visible role, the successful candidate will shape strategy, influence enterprise standards, and partner across sites and functions to strengthen compliance, standardize processes, improve environmental performance, and enable safe, reliable operations across the business.  
  
This role is ideal for a senior environmental leader who brings deep technical expertise, sound business judgment, and the ability to drive impact across a complex, matrixed organization – translating complex regulatory requirements into clear, practical, and scalable processes that support both compliance excellence and operational execution.  
  
Success in this role requires a demonstrated ability to work across functional teams to achieve environmental and compliance objectives; strong problem-solving, project management, planning, organizational, time management, and analytical skills; and strong communication skills, including the ability to translate technical environmental risks and requirements for non-technical audiences and influence positive behavioral change.  
  
This position will require up to 30% travel.

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities:**

* Lead enterprise direction for hazardous waste and dangerous goods compliance, including development and execution of short- and long-term goals and objectives for the EHS function.
* Develop, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise standard work for waste characterization, container management, labeling, storage, inspection, manifesting, and vendor qualification.
* Provide technical environmental support, practical guidance, and compliance solutions to GE Aerospace sites on hazardous waste and dangerous goods requirements.
* Monitor environmental programs for compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, and recommend business-level environmental policies, programs, and improvement initiatives.
* Represent GE Aerospace with governmental environmental agencies and trade/professional associations to support regulatory interpretation and compliance alignment.
* Track environmental performance metrics and drive actions that improve compliance and operating performance.
* Prepare comments on proposed environmental regulations and assess potential business impacts.
* Support sites with waste determinations, supporting documentation, analytical methods, and compliance execution.
* Participate in internal and external compliance audits and support audit readiness, inspection response, CAPA development, and closure verification for recurring or material findings.
* Provide governance for dangerous goods/hazmat transportation, including classification, packaging, marking, labeling, shipping papers, modal requirements, training controls, and shipment readiness reviews.
* Review trends from incidents, near misses, shipment errors, permit events, and vendor performance to identify risks and prioritize preventive actions.
* Lead practical training and coaching for site EHS operations, with a focus on common failure modes and effective controls.

* Partner with site EHS, legal, operations, quality, and logistics teams to interpret requirements and implement practical controls aligned to site processes.
* Estimated travel required is about 30%

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
* Minimum of 5 years of industry experience in environmental compliance, hazardous waste, dangerous goods, or related EHS disciplines.
* Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to environmental operations in the geographic regions where GE Aerospace operates.
* Experience working with complex dangerous goods and hazardous waste regulations.

**Desired Characteristics and Experience:**

* 15+ years of industry experience
* Bachelor's degree in environmental or engineering, an advanced technical degree, and/or Professional Engineer (PE) license
* Experience with Hazardous Secondary Materials

* Enterprise mindset with the ability to connect regulatory requirements to practical business execution
* Ability to simplify complex technical topics into clear expectations and actions
* Passion for building capability, strengthening standard work, and driving sustainable results.

* Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn
* Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively
* Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed
* Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative
* Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker

The base pay range for this position is $157,000 - $210,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 13, 2026.

GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. * **Shape Victoria’s environmental science and public health strategy**
* **Build high-value research, government and industry partnerships**
* **Translate leading science and research into regulatory innovation**
  

**About the organisation**

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is Victoria’s environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on Victorians and their environment. EPA is a values and purpose-driven organisation that works with community, government and industry to deliver for all Victorians. As an independent statutory authority, EPA uses its powers and tools to prevent risks to the environment and human health.

  

**About the role**

As Deputy Chief Environmental Scientist, Science and Public Health Strategy and Partnerships, you will lead EPA’s Science Strategy, Partnerships and Public Health branch, driving sustainable operations and partnerships, technical leadership of science research and development strategy, regulatory innovation and environmental public health influence. Reporting to the Chief Environmental Scientist, you will provide senior executive support and strategic advice on complex science, public health and partnership matters, and represent EPA externally when required. You will provide executive sponsorship for EPA’s Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation model, build high-value partnerships across universities, research institutes, government, industry and health agencies, and lead the development of EPA’s science, digital innovation and environmental public health strategies. Taking a One Health lens, you will integrate science, engineering and research capabilities to strengthen environmental and public health outcomes.

  

**About you**

You are an established scientific and environmental public health leader with extensive experience integrating multidisciplinary health, environmental science and engineering disciplines to translate evidence into strategy and action. You have demonstrated senior executive leadership experience in a complex scientific, public health or regulatory environment and the capability to act as a trusted deputy to a chief scientist or equivalent executive. You bring experience developing strategy, establishing priorities, managing risk and translating strategic direction into practical delivery, together with experience in major research programs, centres of excellence or strategic partnership models. You can influence senior stakeholders, negotiate complex outcomes and clearly communicate scientific, environmental public health and strategic issues to executive, governing board, government, partners and public audiences. A doctorate or relevant postgraduate qualification in environmental public health or a related discipline is required.

**Principal Consultant / Technical Director – Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment**

  

Lead Technical Excellence. Shape Strategy. Grow a Market-Leading Practice.

Are you an established **Ecotoxicologist or Ecological Risk Assessor** looking for an opportunity to build your profile, influence major projects, and help shape the future direction of a growing environmental consultancy practice?

  

We are seeking an experienced **Principal Consultant or Technical Director** to join and lead our **Ecotoxicology and Ecological Risk Assessment group as part of the Toxicology & Risk team** . This is a key technical and business role for a recognised industry professional with a strong technical reputation, established client relationships, and a passion for growing business and developing people.

  

As a key member within our **Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology and Risk Practice** , you will work alongside a highly regarded team of specialist consultants, including a dedicated ecotoxicology group and a broader multidisciplinary practice of more than 40+ experts across Asia Pacific.

  

This is more than a technical leadership role. It is an opportunity to join a collaborative team that combines deep technical expertise with a strong growth mindset. You will have the autonomy to shape the direction of the ecotoxicology practice while being supported by a substantial multidisciplinary network of specialists who are solving some of the most complex environmental challenges across the region.

  

We have just over 1,200 staff in Asia Pacific and you will find us located in all the major cities and many regional areas. We are open to location for the successful person where we have established offices in place.

  

**Responsibilities**

Working with other technical specialists who are passionate about their fields and highly collaborative employees, this role offers the platform to:

  

* Lead and grow a successful ecotoxicology and ecological risk assessment capability.
* Drive business development and work-winning initiatives across existing and emerging markets.
* Leverage your professional network and industry profile to identify opportunities and develop long-term client partnerships.
* Provide technical leadership on complex environmental, contaminated land, mining, industrial, infrastructure and regulatory projects.
* Mentor and develop a team of talented ecotoxicologists and risk assessment specialists.
* Collaborate with leading experts across contaminated land, geochemistry, toxicology, human health risk assessment, hydrogeology and environmental sciences.
Influence strategic direction, service offerings and market growth within a well-established environmental consulting business.  

  

**Experience**

Not only will you be a honest, trusted and great person to be around, you will also be a recognised technical leader who brings:

  

* Relevant tertiary qualifications in ecotoxicology, environmental science, ecology, toxicology or a related discipline coupled with 10-15+ years’ experience ( *ideally within a consulting environment but open to other industry)*
* A strong reputation within industry, regulatory, government and/or commercial sectors.
* Demonstrated success in winning work, developing client relationships and generating revenue growth.
* Established networks and connections that can contribute to the continued expansion of the practice.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and mentoring technical professionals.
* Strong commercial acumen and the ability to identify and capitalise on market opportunities.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.  

  

**Our Benefits**

We are most proud of our expert teams and unique culture where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients.

  

Whether you’re enjoying our flexible hybrid work environment, taking advantage of our novated leasing offers, or at a time in your life where a supportive and generous parental leave scheme is key, our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

  

You can find a comprehensive list **here.**

new_jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

The Environmental Program Leader – Hazardous Waste and Dangerous Goods Compliance will provide enterprise leadership, technical expertise, and continuous improvement across hazardous waste management and dangerous goods/hazmat transportation. In this highly visible role, the successful candidate will shape strategy, influence enterprise standards, and partner across sites and functions to strengthen compliance, standardize processes, improve environmental performance, and enable safe, reliable operations across the business.  
  
This role is ideal for a senior environmental leader who brings deep technical expertise, sound business judgment, and the ability to drive impact across a complex, matrixed organization – translating complex regulatory requirements into clear, practical, and scalable processes that support both compliance excellence and operational execution.  
  
Success in this role requires a demonstrated ability to work across functional teams to achieve environmental and compliance objectives; strong problem-solving, project management, planning, organizational, time management, and analytical skills; and strong communication skills, including the ability to translate technical environmental risks and requirements for non-technical audiences and influence positive behavioral change.  
  
This position will require up to 30% travel.

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities:**

* Lead enterprise direction for hazardous waste and dangerous goods compliance, including development and execution of short- and long-term goals and objectives for the EHS function.
* Develop, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise standard work for waste characterization, container management, labeling, storage, inspection, manifesting, and vendor qualification.
* Provide technical environmental support, practical guidance, and compliance solutions to GE Aerospace sites on hazardous waste and dangerous goods requirements.
* Monitor environmental programs for compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, and recommend business-level environmental policies, programs, and improvement initiatives.
* Represent GE Aerospace with governmental environmental agencies and trade/professional associations to support regulatory interpretation and compliance alignment.
* Track environmental performance metrics and drive actions that improve compliance and operating performance.
* Prepare comments on proposed environmental regulations and assess potential business impacts.
* Support sites with waste determinations, supporting documentation, analytical methods, and compliance execution.
* Participate in internal and external compliance audits and support audit readiness, inspection response, CAPA development, and closure verification for recurring or material findings.
* Provide governance for dangerous goods/hazmat transportation, including classification, packaging, marking, labeling, shipping papers, modal requirements, training controls, and shipment readiness reviews.
* Review trends from incidents, near misses, shipment errors, permit events, and vendor performance to identify risks and prioritize preventive actions.
* Lead practical training and coaching for site EHS operations, with a focus on common failure modes and effective controls.

* Partner with site EHS, legal, operations, quality, and logistics teams to interpret requirements and implement practical controls aligned to site processes.
* Estimated travel required is about 30%

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
* Minimum of 5 years of industry experience in environmental compliance, hazardous waste, dangerous goods, or related EHS disciplines.
* Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to environmental operations in the geographic regions where GE Aerospace operates.
* Experience working with complex dangerous goods and hazardous waste regulations.

**Desired Characteristics and Experience:**

* 15+ years of industry experience
* Bachelor's degree in environmental or engineering, an advanced technical degree, and/or Professional Engineer (PE) license
* Experience with Hazardous Secondary Materials

* Enterprise mindset with the ability to connect regulatory requirements to practical business execution
* Ability to simplify complex technical topics into clear expectations and actions
* Passion for building capability, strengthening standard work, and driving sustainable results.

* Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn
* Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively
* Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed
* Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative
* Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker

The base pay range for this position is $157,000 - $210,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 13, 2026.

GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants.
